analysis: HadCRUT5 member-specific global annual trend distribution

ensemble_mean_series.hac_note: Conditional residual-based uncertainty; not a replacement for member-level trend distribution.

coverage_metadata.limitation: The annual coverage uncertainty series is official and retained separately; its interannual covariance is not supplied here, so no exact coverage-error slope distribution is claimed.
coverage_metadata.coverage_trend_bound_interpretation: Covariance-agnostic RMS upper bound from Minkowski's inequality using the 47 published annual coverage 1-sigma values and OLS slope weights. This is not a confidence interval or a point estimate of coverage trend error.

summary_series_comparison.note: Rounding/processing differences are reported, not silently corrected.

coverage_uncertainty_internal_consistenc.method: Infer total_sigma from the published 2.5%-97.5% interval using 1.96, then subtract the annual 200-member sample variance in quadrature.
coverage_uncertainty_internal_consistenc.interpretation: Internal consistency check across official HadCRUT5 summary and ensemble CSVs; it does not independently reproduce the ERA5 coverage-error model.

method_notes: Each of the 200 annual global member series is fitted independently over the same 47 complete years, 1979-2025.
OLS slope is expressed in degrees Celsius per decade; a constant anomaly baseline shift does not alter it.
The empirical 2.5th-97.5th percentile interval describes the spread of member-specific slopes, preserving temporal covariance within each member series.
This interval is not a frequentist confidence interval for the OLS regression coefficient.
The additional coverage uncertainty is not folded into member-specific slope percentiles because its time dependence is not modeled here.

Official annual coverage uncertainty values are cross-checked against the published 95% summary-series limits and the 200-member sample standard deviation; the quadrature reconstruction agrees within rounding.
A covariance-agnostic RMS upper bound for coverage contribution to the 1979-2025 OLS slope is reported using the annual 1-sigma coverage values. It is a mathematical bound, not a confidence interval.
